messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: routing anomaly detected — sudden spike in assignment failures and 403s from dedicated pools for tenant `mercantile-inc`. Threshold breached at 03:14 UTC
ravi: i'm pulling routing/eval logs now
zoe: saw the alert, looks like hosted requests getting routed into dedicated pools despite dedicated `tenant_allowlist` set
talia: timeline? when did the new policy go out?
ops-bot: deploy: routing-policy v3.2.0 deployed at 03:09:12 UTC by ci/cd
sam: ok new policy landed at 03:09. errors spike at 03:13. policy diff incoming
ravi: diff snippet:
```
- tenant_guard: enforce
+ tenant_guard: enabled=false
```
ravi: uh, that toggle flips semantics. enabled=false effectively disables tenant guard
zoe: that would allow cross-tenant allocations into dedicated pools if fallback rules hit
eng-oncall: paging runtime and ops. i'm taking lead for mitigation
eng-oncall: immediate mitigations?
talia: options: 1) rollback routing-policy to v3.1.8 2) emergency hotfix to routing-service to re-enable tenant guard 3) add runtime safety check to reject assignment if tenant mismatch
sam: rollback is lowest-risk and fastest. who can roll back now? @luis?
luis: doing rollback now: `kubectl -n routing rollout undo deployment/routing-service --to-revision=256`
ops-bot: rollback initiated by luis
ops-bot: rollback completed at 03:22:05 UTC
zoe: telemetry post-rollback: dedicated 403s down from 95/min -> 4/min within 4m
ravi: but we still see some oscillation: region fallback loop between us-west and eu-west for certain requests, causing repeated evaluations and extra load
eng-oncall: paste an example trace
ravi: ```
[03:13:15] req=xyz tenant=mercantile-inc eval=v3.2.0 -> fallback_to_region eu-west
[03:13:16] eval=v3.2.0 -> tenant_guard check skipped due to `tenant_guard` flag false
[03:13:16] assign -> dedicated-pool-3 (tenant not listed) -> 403 from runtime
[03:13:17] client retry -> eval -> fallback back to us-west -> assign -> dedicated-pool-1 -> 403 -> back to eu-west ...
```
talia: looks like eval ordering changed in v3.2.0: region fallback rules now run before tenant guard, which combined with the disabled guard caused oscillation
eng-oncall: mitigation summary: rollback completed, runtime guard hotfix deployed, and we rate-limited routing-service to reduce storming
ops-bot: runtime hotfix deployed at 03:30:09 UTC
zoe: hotfix snippet added into runtime: 
```python
# runtime safety: enforce tenant isolation regardless of policy flags
if pool.is_dedicated and not pool.is_allowed(tenant_id):
    raise AssignmentError("tenant isolation enforced at runtime")
```
sam: metrics after safety patch: failed assignments reduced to baseline, overall error-rate normalized by 03:34
pm-nora: customer impact: `mercantile-inc` experienced degraded SLA (~9 minutes of errors/latency). Secondary customers: `shopwise` small percentage of requests errored
pm-nora: initiating customer comms and scheduling a tech sync with mercantile-inc CSM
security-bot: quick check: any sign of successful data access across tenant boundaries?
zoe: initial audit: no successful cross-tenant reads, errors were access_denied/assignment failures and cache mismatches
eng-oncall: creating incident ticket INC-9011 for postmortem and follow-ups
luis: blocking items in ticket:
- revert ambiguous `tenant_guard` flag from v3.2.0 schema
- add unit+integration tests for rule ordering (tenant_guard before region_fallback)
- require canary rollout of routing-policy at 0.5% traffic for 30m before full rollout
- add runtime guard as permanent defense-in-depth
- run audit across dedicated pools to confirm no mis-assignments persisted
pm-nora: customer message draft: "We experienced a routing policy regression that briefly allowed requests for some hosted customers to be routed into dedicated pools, triggering errors. We rolled back the policy, deployed a runtime safety patch, and are investigating root cause and remediation steps. We will follow up with a detailed postmortem and offer credits." ok to send?
mercantile-inc (via CSM): please confirm if any data was exposed and whether you'll prevent recurrence
zoe: replied to CSM: no data exfiltration detected, we added runtime guard and will deliver postmortem + mitigation plan
eng-oncall: timeline to capture:
- 03:09:12 UTC: routing-policy v3.2.0 deploy
- 03:13:00 UTC: start of error spike
- 03:22:05 UTC: rollback to v3.1.8 complete
- 03:30:09 UTC: runtime safety patch deployed
- 03:34:00 UTC: error rates back to baseline
eng-oncall: estimated scope: ~610 failed assignments total across 9 minutes, peak ~88 tps during spike
ops-bot: incident marked mitigated at 03:36:00 UTC by eng-oncall
eng-oncall: postmortem owners: zoe (eng), nora (prod), luis (ops)
security-bot: add security review to postmortem: validate no tenant access occurred and sign off
sam: quick follow-ups: add regression test for flag inversion, add ordering tests, update schema to avoid boolean negation ambiguity, and add canary gating in deployment pipeline
pm-nora: assigning follow-up tickets and scheduling postmortem writeup in #postmortems
eng-oncall: handing off to postmortem channel. good triage and rollback work everyone.
